To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the noise and the velocity fluctuations of a jet are correlated, that the cross-spectrum between the noise and the flow is a measure of jet noise, and that the cross-spectral density of the flow and noise is consistent with the postu- lated source mechanism.

the cross-correlations between LDV measurements of the flow and the farfield noise show a strong coherence, and that the cross-spectra of the LDV and noise are in excellent agreement with the theoretical predictions of Ribner's shear and self noise theories.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of cross-correlation and cross-spectrum functions between jet noise and the flow.
the direct correlation of jet flow with far-field noise.
the development of a new diagnostic tool for jet noise studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LDV-jet correlations are consistent with the self and shear noise models and with theory.
the source model and the jet flow are consistent with the observed noise.
the LDV-jet correlations provide a direct measure of the source terms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the noise and flow correlations have been successfully demonstrated.
a new technique for measuring the flow of a jet was developed and used in conjunction with the jet noise to determine the noise source distribution.
we have demonstrated the existence of a one-to-one relationship between the postulated sources and the radiated noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet flow can be directly measured using LDV and correlated with the far-field noise.
the noise and flow are directly correlated.
we can measure the coherence between a jet flow and jet noise.
